film: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
section_title: One More Round With the Final Girl
connection: Jane Schoenbrun's meta-slasher hands a young director the keys to a dead franchise — <cite index="13-2">a "zombie IP," the "Little Death" franchise, a riff on Jason Voorhees, complete with a fictional camp called Miasma and a masked villain</cite> — and sends her after the woman who survived the original massacre. The plot is literally a comeback: <cite index="15-1">Kris journeys to the movie's iced-over summer camp to track down its original final girl, Billy (Gillian Anderson), and convince her to star in the remake.</cite> Critics have noted that Hannah Einbinder's character herself gets pulled into the role, since <cite index="11-1">through the film's surreal twists and turns, she effectively becomes a kind of final girl, even if it's not quite as simple as that.</cite>
training_tie_in: A final girl is a fighter who already survived one brutal night and swore she was done — and the movie's entire engine is a promoter showing up years later, dangling a payday, to talk her back into the ring where she got cut open the first time. That's the journeyman's whole career: the body keeps the scar tissue and the tape, but somebody always has a reason to book one more fight in the same building. Camp Miasma just makes literal what every veteran boxer already knows — the rematch you thought was behind you is usually the one that finds you.
